articles.title: Amit Shah flags off India's first LNG-powered train from Ahmedabad's Sabarmati Station
articles.content: Ahmedabad ( Gujarat ) [India], September 27 (ANI): Union Home Minister Amit Shah flagged off the country's first LNG (Liquefied Natural Gas)-powered train from Ahmedabad's Sabarmati Railway Station on Sunday, alongside launching several other Indian Railways projects in the Sabarmati Division. Speaking on the occasion, Shah said the projects addressed environmental concerns, passenger convenience and safety. "Today marks the launch of various Indian Railways projects within the Sabarmati Division. These initiatives address environmental concerns, enhance passenger convenience, and bolster safety. In the past, I have frequently disembarked at Sabarmati Railway Station while travelling from Delhi. I extend my heartiest congratulations to the entire team, from the Sabarmati Railway Division to Railway Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw, because seeing Sabarmati Station now, after so long, is remarkable," he said. Shah added that the station and its facilities had undergone a complete transformation with an investment of ₹1,472 crore. "A radical transformation has been achieved regarding passenger convenience, safety, and connectivity. The projects inaugurated and those for which foundation stones were laid today, involving an investment of ₹1,472 crore, will prove immensely beneficial for passengers in this region," he said. Highlighting the Railways' progress on reducing diesel dependency and expanding electrification, Shah said the railways' consumption of diesel has dropped from 293 crore litres to 108 crore. He stated, "In 2015-16, the railways consumed 293 crore litres of diesel. That figure has now dropped to 108 crore in 2024-25, and by 2030, we will bring it down to zero, thereby saving Indian currency. This is a massive achievement that often goes unnoticed." He further said, "Electrification covered just 75 kilometres in 2010-11, whereas in 2023-24, we electrified 7,188 kilometres in a single year. 99.6 per cent of the railway network is already electrified. We will complete the remaining 0.3 per cent as well. Only Sweden has achieved 100 per cent electrification globally, but there is a tenfold difference between the scale of Sweden's rail network and ours." Shah also took a swipe at the Congress over its track record on development. "The people of this country should question the Congress members, who spout all sorts of nonsense, about this vast disparity in development. In their last ten years, they did nothing but engage in scams, scandals, and corruption amounting to ₹12 lakh crore; yet, in 12 years, no one has been able to level even the slightest allegation of corruption against PM Modi," he said. Earlier in the day, Shah also attended a programme organised on the occasion of Acharya Shri Padmasagar Surishwar Ji Maharaj's 92nd birthday in Ahmedabad. (ANI)

articles.title: Amit Shah launches India's first LNG train today alongside railway projects worth over ... - Swarajya
articles.content: Sep 27, 2026 | Updated 05:07 PM GMT+5:30 Save & read from anywhere! Bookmark stories for easy access on any device or the Swarajya app . Union Home Minister Amit Shah flagged off India's first liquefied natural gas-powered train from Sabarmati Station today. The event also saw the launch of railway projects worth over Rs 1,542 crore, with Gujarat Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel, Deputy Chief Minister Harsh Sanghavi and other regional leaders in attendance. For the first time in Indian Railways, an LNG-based fuel system has been successfully adopted in the train's Driving Power Cars. Two 1,400-horsepower Driving Power Cars at Sabarmati Integrated Coaching Depot have been converted into a diesel-LNG dual-fuel system, with LNG replacing nearly 40 per cent of diesel consumption. The technology allows the same engine to use both LNG and diesel, providing operational flexibility. Both converted power cars completed over 2,000 km of successful field trials to ensure safety and efficiency. Each Driving Power Car has been fitted with an LNG tank with a capacity of around 2,200 litres, holding approximately 950-1,000 kg of usable LNG, with a full tank providing enough fuel for around 444 km of daily operation. The LNG initiative is expected to reduce fuel costs and lower emissions of carbon dioxide, nitrogen oxides and particulate matter. Additional projects include the inauguration of the WAG-12 Sabarmati locomotive maintenance shed, an automatic block signalling system on the Sabarmati-Kalol-Bhandu Motidau and Sabarmati-Sanand-Jakhwada sections, and the doubling of the Sabarmati-Sarkhej railway line. The foundation stone was also laid for the indigenous Kavach safety system on Ahmedabad-Palanpur and Ahmedabad-Samakhiyali sections. The newly developed WAG-12 locomotive maintenance shed, constructed at an estimated cost of Rs 700 crore, will provide maintenance facilities for 300 high-horsepower electric locomotives designed for transporting heavy freight trains. articles.title: India's First LNG Train To Be Flagged Off Today; Know How The Dual-Fuel System Works
articles.content: Home / India / Trending / India’s First LNG Train To Be Flagged Off Today; Know How The Dual-Fuel System Works The DEMU train can use both LNG and diesel, as the dual-fuel system is designed to maintain the engine’s power and operating performance. by Tanvi Shrivastava Updated: September 27, 2026 11:49 AM Share Cover Image Courtesy: Wikimedia Commons India’s first LNG-diesel dual-fuel DEMU train is set to be formally flagged off from Gujarat’s Sabarmati railway station on September 27. The train uses a dual-fuel system that lets its engine run on both LNG (liquefied natural gas) and diesel, switching between the two depending on fuel availability. The technology aims to reduce diesel consumption while promoting cleaner, alternative fuels in Indian Railways. Scroll down to know more. India’s First LNG-Diesel Dual-Fuel DEMU Train Flags Off Today According to a report by The Indian Express, the project has been developed through the conversion of two 1,400 HP Driving Power Cars (DPCs) at the Sabarmati depot. The converted power cars have completed more than 2,000 km of field trials, which were conducted to assess the performance and reliability of the dual-fuel system. The technology can replace up to around 40% of diesel consumption with LNG. The train is being operated by the Ahmedabad Division of Western Railway. During its formal launch, it is scheduled to operate from Sabarmati towards Mahesana. The eight-coach DEMU consists of non-AC chair-car coaches. Unlike a train that runs entirely on LNG, this DEMU can use both LNG and diesel. The engine can switch between the two fuels depending on availability, allowing operations to continue even when LNG is not available. The dual-fuel system has been designed to maintain the engine’s power and operating performance while reducing diesel consumption. Each converted DPC is fitted with an LNG tank with a capacity of around 2,200 litres, with approximately 950–1,000 kg of usable LNG. According to the approved design, a fully loaded tank can support around 444 km of operation under the specified conditions. Also Read: Delhi-Siliguri Bullet Train: 20-Hour Journey Could Drop To 6 Hours 45 Minutes LNG Train To Reduce Fuel Costs And Emissions The use of LNG is expected to reduce diesel consumption as well as emissions such as carbon dioxide (CO₂), nitrogen oxides (NOx) and particulate matter. Indian Railways estimates annual fuel savings of around ₹11.9 lakh per DPC, while an eight-coach rake with two DPCs could save approximately ₹23.9 lakh annually, based on trial estimates. The initiative is part of Indian Railways’ efforts to reduce dependence on diesel and explore alternative fuels for railway operations. The successful trials and subsequent passenger operations at Sabarmati mark an important step in testing LNG as a fuel option for DEMU services. articles.title: APSEZ's Dhamra Port becomes India's first large-scale private multi-cargo port to run fully on ...
articles.content: NEW DELHI, Sept 27: Dhamra Port in Odisha, operated by Adani Ports and Special Economic Zone (APSEZ), has shifted its entire electricity consumption to renewable power, becoming India's first large-scale private multi-cargo port to operate fully on renewable electricity, according to the company. The port, which handles more than 48 million tonnes (MT) of cargo annually, now meets more than 90 lakh units of monthly electricity demand from renewable sources. At its current operating level, its renewable power consumption exceeds 108 gigawatt-hours (GWh) on an annualised basis, APSEZ said. The shift, effective August 2026, is part of APSEZ's long-term Net-Zero strategy and is expected to reduce emissions associated with purchased electricity while improving the environmental performance of the energy-intensive port operations. The transition has been achieved through a combination of captive renewable power, third-party access arrangements and green-power procurement under Odisha's regulatory framework. About 25-30 per cent of Dhamra's renewable electricity comes from APSEZ's captive hybrid power plant at Khavda in Gujarat, while another 10-15 per cent is sourced through third-party access. The remaining requirement is met through a Green Consumer arrangement with Odisha's distribution utility. Renewable electricity now powers round-the-clock operations at the port, including cargo handling, storage, rail-linked activities and other critical infrastructure. Dhamra, located on the Odisha coast between Haldia and Paradip, is one of eastern India's key deep-draft ports. It has an installed capacity of 60 MT and handled 48.8 MT of cargo in the financial year ended March 2026. The port has six dry-cargo berths, rapid-loading silos, wagon tipplers, track hoppers, mechanised storage yards and jetty equipment, along with rail and road connectivity to mineral-rich hinterlands across Odisha, Jharkhand and West Bengal. The move makes Dhamra the latest large-scale industrial and logistics facility to increase its reliance on renewable electricity as companies seek to reduce emissions from operations and meet longer-term decarbonisation targets. (PTI)

articles.title: IIT Delhi builds India's first working indigenous micro-GPU for low-cost displays, fishing ...
articles.content: Home Trending News IIT Delhi builds India’s first working indigenous micro-GPU for low-cost displays, fishing boats & e-book readers IIT Delhi builds India’s first working indigenous micro-GPU for low-cost displays, fishing boats & e-book readers By developing an indigenous micro-GPU architecture, the IIT Delhi team is working towards a graphics processing solution that could eventually support affordable embedded computing applications. By Devanshu Srivastava 26 Sep 2026 Follow Us New Update A glimpse of the IIT Delhi campus and a micro-GPU IIT Delhi researchers have developed what the institute describes as India’s first working, indigenously designed micro-GPU. The project was developed by M.Tech students Nammi Akash and M. Ravi Teja under the guidance of Prof. Jayadeva and Prof. Kaushik Saha of the Electrical Engineering Department and was demonstrated on a standard Spartan 7 FPGA development board by rendering graphics. The researchers said the development demonstrates the potential of programmable graphics hardware for building affordable computing platforms. According to the researchers, the micro-GPU is designed for devices that require basic graphics and display capabilities. Advertisment Add Startup Pedia As A Trusted Source Unlike large GPUs used in high-end computers, the micro-GPU is designed for applications where a smaller, more affordable graphics processing solution is suitable. What is a Micro-GPU and Where Can it be Used? A micro-GPU ( Graphics Processing Unit ) is a smaller, programmable graphics processor designed to handle graphics-related tasks in embedded systems and other devices. The IIT Delhi team demonstrated its micro-GPU on a Spartan 7 FPGA board, where it rendered graphics. The design has been developed so that it can eventually be implemented on programmable hardware such as FPGAs or incorporated into a chip. The researchers see several possible applications for the technology. These include industrial display systems, simple human-machine interfaces, e-rickshaw dashboard navigators, navigation terminals for small fishing boats, and educational e-book readers. The technology is therefore aimed at everyday and specialised devices that require basic graphics processing rather than high-performance computing or gaming applications. Prof. Jayadeva said the project involved several innovations to implement the design on a standard FPGA board. The work also brings together arithmetic hardware, programmable architectures, compilers, and embedded systems concepts within a single framework. Also read: "Stuff that happened in 2014": Telegram trolls WhatsApp over usernames rollout, claims it did it first IIT Delhi Team Plans Larger Graphics Processor The team is now working on a larger 8- to 16-core graphics processor architecture. Alongside the hardware development, the researchers are also working on an optimised compiler and software tools that can work with the processor. The team is further exploring a proof of concept using a 65nm chip-making process. It plans to seek funding for chip development, system integration, and eventual commercialisation. The researchers said their objective was to create a compact but genuinely programmable graphics processing architecture suitable for FPGA implementation and future ASIC realisation.
